translations.translatedText: # Tuesday 21.2.2020 (radio)
Less and less cash is used for payments. The coronavirus is spreading in China. Police will get more body cameras. Helsinki is the busiest port in Europe.
## Cash payments are decreasing
![A customer pays at a self-service checkout in a shop.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-10617452)
Open image viewer
Most people pay by card in shops. Photo: Heini Holopainen / Yle
People pay with cash less than before. The use of cash has fallen a lot in 10 years.
About 10 per cent of Finns now use cash. Only 10 years ago about 30 per cent of Finns used cash.
Now a lot is paid for by bank card, for example. Experts say that with this you do not always notice how the money is being spent as well as when you pay in cash.
## The coronavirus is spreading in China

![In the Chinese capital Beijing, tourists are visiting Tiananmen Square as usual. A man has put on a face mask. A little over 200 new coronavirus infections have been confirmed in the country, and three people have died from the disease.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_6319,h_3554,x_0,y_663/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-6331765e25d49b7cf51/1579592852)
Open image viewer
A man put on a face mask in the Chinese capital, Beijing. Photo: EPA

There have been more coronavirus infections in China. There are 80 new infections. Almost 300 people have fallen ill with the disease that the coronavirus causes. 6 people have already died from the disease.

Chinese people are travelling a lot now, because many go to visit relatives to celebrate the Chinese New Year. In China and other Asian countries, temperature checks of passengers have started, for example at airports, railway stations and bus stations. Feverish people can be identified with thermal cameras.
The World Health Organization, WHO, is holding an emergency meeting on Wednesday because of the spread of the coronavirus.
## Body cameras for police across Finland
![police officer with body camera](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9580397)
Open image viewer
A body camera records what the police officer sees. Photo: Berislav Jurišić / Yle
The police are introducing body cameras across the whole country. A small camera is attached to the police officer's uniform, which records on video what is in front of the police officer.

A body camera adds to the safety of police officers. Many people are calmer when they know that a police body camera is recording. The police can use the video footage as evidence if the video records, for example, a fight or someone attacking a police officer.
Body cameras have been tested by the Helsinki Police Department for 4 years. This year, body cameras will be bought for all police departments in Finland.
## Helsinki is the busiest port in Europe
![Cruise ships at the South Harbour in Helsinki](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11069064)
Open image viewer
Ships at the South Harbour in Helsinki. Photo: Henrietta Hassinen / Yle

The port of Helsinki is the busiest passenger port in Europe. Over 12 million ferry passengers went through it last year. That is more than in other ports in Europe. The port of Helsinki has been the busiest passenger port in Europe for 3 years now.
Most of the passengers at the port of Helsinki go to or come from Tallinn. A lot of passengers also travel to Stockholm every day.
A lot of foreign cruise ships also visited the port of Helsinki last year. Over 300 of them visited.
